text: Always runs ( if: always() ), needs every other job, and fails if any of them failed or was cancelled. This is the single required status check on main , so jobs can be added or renamed in the workflow file without touching branch protection. skipped counts as a pass on purpose, so future if: -filtered jobs don't false-fail the gate.

text: Triggered on push to main with the path filter skills/** , so docs-only or workflow-only merges don't run it. The workflow grants packages: write only to this job and uses the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN . No PAT, no org secret. Check out the full history ( fetch-depth: 0 ) so the diff against the previous commit works. Install uv (third-party action, SHA-pinned per the policy below). Re-validate every skill with uv run python scripts/validate_skill.py --all , the final check before any package bytes leave the repo. Set up Node with the registry pointed at https://npm.pkg.github.com and the @bcgov scope. (The exact Node version lives in the workflow file.) Run .github/scripts/publish-changed-skills.sh , which diffs BEFORE_SHA against HEAD_SHA , walks each changed skill, and runs npm publish --tag latest with NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} . The --tag latest keeps the latest dist-tag pointed at the just-shipped version, so npm install @bcgov/<name> (no version) always pulls the most recent release. Already-published versions are skipped. A merge that doesn't bump a skill's package.json version is a no-op for that skill, so re-publishing is impossible by design. Bumping the version is what ships a release. See Versioning .

text: Dependabot opens grouped upgrade PRs with Conventional Commit prefixes. Cadence and ecosystems are configured in .github/dependabot.yml . When the PR's author is dependabot[bot] , an in-repo workflow approves it and turns on auto-merge, so it squash-merges itself the moment the same results check goes green. If the upgrade breaks something, results stays red and the PR sits there until a human looks at it. The auto-merge workflow lives alongside the rest of CI under .github/workflows/ . The merge gate it has to clear is exactly the one humans clear: there is no special path around results , and the workflow itself only acts on PRs Dependabot opened.

text: Skills are published as npm packages to GitHub Packages under the @bcgov scope. Installing one is five steps: configure the registry, authenticate, install, wire the skill into your agent, and (later) upgrade. The SKILL.md format follows the agentskills.io open standard, so the same install flow works for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and any other agent that loads SKILL.md manifests. GitHub Packages always requires authentication , even for public packages on the npm registry. This is a GitHub Packages behaviour, not a permission setting on this repo. The flow below uses the GitHub CLI to mint a short-lived token, so you don't need to manage a personal access token.

text: One line. The installer checks for the GitHub CLI (and installs it if missing), adds the read:packages scope, writes the project .npmrc , runs npm install , and offers to wire the skill into your agent (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or a custom location for Codex / Cursor / Cline / etc.). Re-run any time to install another skill or upgrade an existing one. Supply-chain note — pin to an immutable ref in production. The forms below default to main , which is mutable: the installer code can change between when you read it and when you run it. For CI, scripted setup, or any environment where reproducibility matters, replace main with a 40-char commit SHA you have audited — pick the latest green commit from bcgov/agent-skills/commits/main/scripts . This matches the advice our own github-actions skill gives for third-party Actions. # macOS / Linux (interactive prompts work via process substitution) # Pinned (recommended) -- replace <SHA> with a 40-char commit you have reviewed: bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bcgov/agent-skills/<SHA>/scripts/install-skill.sh) # Rolling (convenient for one-off installs -- may change without notice): bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bcgov/agent-skills/main/scripts/install-skill.sh) # Windows (PowerShell) works on PS 5.1 and PS 7 with no ExecutionPolicy change # Pinned (recommended) -- replace <SHA> with a 40-char commit you have reviewed: & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bcgov/agent-skills/<SHA>/scripts/install-skill.ps1))) # Rolling (convenient for one-off installs -- may change without notice): & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bcgov/agent-skills/main/scripts/install-skill.ps1))) Prefer to audit the script before running it? Pin to a SHA, download, read, then run. When you pin to a commit SHA, GitHub serves the exact blob that was committed at that ref — the SHA itself is the integrity anchor; there is no separate published hash to compare against. Recording a sha256sum is useful for your own change-management trail (so re-deploys can detect drift), not as a first-time verification step. # macOS / Linux curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bcgov/agent-skills/<SHA>/scripts/install-skill.sh -o install-skill.sh less install-skill.sh # review the code sha256sum install-skill.sh # optional: record with your deploy ticket bash install-skill.sh # Windows (PowerShell) irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bcgov/agent-skills/<SHA>/scripts/install-skill.ps1 -OutFile install-skill.ps1 Get-Content install-skill.ps1 | more # review the code Get-FileHash install-skill.ps1 -Algorithm SHA256 # optional: record with your deploy ticket .\install-skill.ps1 Non-interactive form (CI or scripted setup — passing a positional skill name skips the wire-up prompt automatically): bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bcgov/agent-skills/<SHA>/scripts/install-skill.sh) azure-networking 0.1.1 & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bcgov/agent-skills/<SHA>/scripts/install-skill.ps1))) -Skill azure-networking -Version 0.1.1 Agent compatibility today: only Copilot and Claude Code load SKILL.md natively via the agentskills.io standard. For Codex CLI, Cursor, Cline, Continue.dev, and others, pick “Custom location” in the wire-up prompt and the script symlinks the skill into the folder your tool already scans — see Step 4 for the underlying snippets. Prefer to understand or run each step yourself? The manual flow follows.

sectionTitle: Step 1: Point npm at GitHub Packages
text: Create a project-local .npmrc beside the package.json where you want to consume the skill. The same file works in local dev and GitHub Actions; the only thing that changes is where NODE_AUTH_TOKEN comes from. @bcgov:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN} ${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN} is expanded by npm at install time from the environment variable; the literal string lives in the file, so it's safe to commit.

text: First time only, grant your CLI token the read:packages scope: gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:packages When prompted "Authenticate Git with your GitHub credentials?", answer No if you already have Git auth working (especially SSH commit signing). The prompt is unrelated to npm and answering yes can overwrite Git settings. Every shell session, export the CLI's current token as NODE_AUTH_TOKEN : # PowerShell $env:NODE_AUTH_TOKEN = gh auth token # bash / zsh export NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) Want to revoke npm access later? gh auth logout ends both your gh session and any NODE_AUTH_TOKEN that came from it, so credential management stays in one place.

sectionTitle: Option B: Symlink one skill at a time
text: Some agents only scan a fixed project folder. Symlink each installed package in — the folder name matches the package name, so the link is one-to-one with no renaming. The snippets below assume azure-networking ; substitute any @bcgov/<name> you installed. GitHub Copilot (VS Code) VS Code Copilot auto-discovers project skills under .github/skills/ , .claude/skills/ , or .agents/skills/ ; personal skills live under ~/.copilot/skills/ , ~/.claude/skills/ , or ~/.agents/skills/ . # bash / zsh (from repo root) mkdir -p .github/skills ln -s ../../node_modules/@bcgov/azure-networking .github/skills/azure-networking # PowerShell (from repo root; symlinks need Developer Mode or admin) New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .github\skills | Out-Null New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path .github\skills\azure-networking -Target ..\..\node_modules\@bcgov\azure-networking # Copy instead of symlink (works everywhere, but you re-copy on update) cp -r node_modules/@bcgov/azure-networking .github/skills/azure-networking Copilot picks up the skill on the next chat. Claude Code Claude Code loads project skills from .claude/skills/ and personal skills from ~/.claude/skills/ , and watches the directory so newly linked skills appear in the same session. # bash / zsh (from repo root) mkdir -p .claude/skills ln -s ../../node_modules/@bcgov/azure-networking .claude/skills/azure-networking # PowerShell (from repo root) New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .claude\skills | Out-Null New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path .claude\skills\azure-networking -Target ..\..\node_modules\@bcgov\azure-networking Other agents (Cursor, Claude API, custom loaders) Any agent that loads SKILL.md manifests directly can point at the installed directory: node_modules/@bcgov/<name>/SKILL.md References, scripts, and assets sit next to SKILL.md , so relative links inside the manifest resolve without extra config. For the Claude API Skills beta, pass the same path to the SDK's skill loader; see the anthropics/skills reference repo for the SKILL.md contract and loader examples. GitHub Actions If a workflow runs an agent and needs the skill on disk in the agent's expected location, install and link in the same step: - run: | npm ci mkdir -p .github/skills ln -sf "$(pwd)/node_modules/@bcgov/azure-networking" .github/skills/azure-networking env: NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

text: npm error 401 Unauthorized NODE_AUTH_TOKEN is empty or the token doesn't have read:packages . Re-run gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:packages . Re-export the token in the current shell: $env:NODE_AUTH_TOKEN = gh auth token (PowerShell) or export NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) (bash). Confirm echo $env:NODE_AUTH_TOKEN / echo "$NODE_AUTH_TOKEN" prints a non-empty value. npm error 404 Not Found The version doesn't exist, or the registry is wrong. Check: The catalogue for the published version. Your .npmrc has @bcgov:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com . You're running npm install from the directory containing that .npmrc . npm picks the wrong registry / falls back to npmjs.org Make sure the scope and the auth line both point at GitHub Packages; they must both be present in .npmrc : @bcgov:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN} If you also have a global ~/.npmrc with a different registry= , the scoped registry line wins, but the auth line must match the URL of whatever registry actually serves the install. GitHub Actions: 403 Forbidden when reading the package Your workflow job is missing permissions: packages: read . The default GITHUB_TOKEN permission profile in many orgs only grants contents: read , so npm gets denied. Add the block in the snippet above to the job (not the workflow root — job-scoped permissions override). Can I use a personal access token (PAT) instead of gh auth token ? Yes; a classic PAT with read:packages works in place of the CLI-issued token. The CLI flow is just lower friction (no separate token to generate, rotate, or revoke), and gh auth logout cleans up both your CLI session and any token sourced from it. My agent doesn't see the skill after I linked it in Both VS Code Copilot and Claude Code require the skill's on-disk folder name to match the name field in SKILL.md exactly. With this repo's @bcgov/<name> convention the names line up automatically, but if you renamed a folder or copied with a different name you'll hit a silent skip. Correct: .github/skills/azure-networking → node_modules/@bcgov/azure-networking Wrong: .github/skills/azure-net (folder name doesn't match the manifest name: azure-networking ) → agent ignores the skill In VS Code, run Chat: Open Customizations and check the Skills tab to see whether Copilot picked it up. sectionTitle: Why GitHub Packages and not public npm?
text: A few practical reasons line up: Scoped to the org. The @bcgov scope on GitHub Packages lives inside the same GitHub org that owns the repo, which means the same access surface, audit log, and identity. Public npm would introduce a second account plus another set of tokens to rotate, and one more place where secrets can leak. Token-free CI. Workflows in this org can publish and consume with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN : no bot account, no NPM_TOKEN secret to manage. Right audience. These skills encode BC Gov rules and aren't intended for general public consumption. GitHub Packages keeps the catalogue scoped to the people it was written for, without having to make it private.

sectionTitle: Why does installing a "public" package still need authentication?
text: This is a GitHub Packages behaviour, not a permission on this repo. The npm registry GitHub runs ( npm.pkg.github.com ) requires a token on every install, even for packages anyone can read. There is no anonymous read path. The good news is that the token doesn't have to be sensitive: any GitHub user can mint a short-lived one with gh auth refresh -h github.com -s read:packages , and CI gets one for free via secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN . See Consume → Step 2 .

No "is this PAT still in use anywhere?" graveyard to maintain. If your environment can't run gh (locked-down CI runner, etc.), a classic PAT with read:packages is a drop-in replacement.

It lives in package.json (see §3 ), and that's the one place to set it; don't add a version field to SKILL.md .

text: After the frontmatter, the body MUST contain — in this order — an H1 title followed by all seven ## sections. Each section must have at least one line of content. # <Skill Name> ## Use When - <specific situation> ## Don't Use When - <adjacent case> → <other skill> ## Workflow 1. <step + tool> 2. ... ## Rules - Always <X> - Never <Y> (Why: <non-obvious reason>) ## Examples - "<user phrasing>" → <action> ## Edge Cases - If <lookup empty> → <fallback> ## References See [references/REFERENCE.md](references/REFERENCE.md) for <heavy detail>

text: A SKILL.md is loaded into the agent's context up front, so it must stay skimmable. The manifest is capped at 500 lines (the whole file, frontmatter included). When a skill needs deeper material — long procedures, lookup tables, worked examples, API detail — put it in a references/ file the agent pulls on demand, and link it from the ## References section.

sectionTitle: Keep bundled resources flat: one level deep
text: Skills may ship scripts/ , references/ , and assets/ directories beside the SKILL.md . These must stay exactly one level deep : flat files only, no nested subdirectories. Use references/REFERENCE.md , not references/api/v1/REFERENCE.md . A flat layout keeps on-demand resources predictable for the agent to locate.

text: A contributed skill under skills/ ships as a versioned npm package, so it MUST include a package.json beside its SKILL.md . Meta-skills under .github/skills/ are never published, so a package.json is optional there, and validated only when one is present. Field Type Notes name string Scoped package name ( @bcgov/<skill-name> ) — must match the manifest name so the install path doubles as the agent skill directory. version string Semver ( MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH ). The publish workflow reads this to decide what (if anything) to ship. { "name": "@bcgov/example-skill", "version": "0.1.0", "publishConfig": { "registry": "https://npm.pkg.github.com" } } The entire skill directory is bundled automatically. Do not add a files field; that turns npm into a whitelist and would silently drop directories. To exclude scratch files, add a .npmignore inside the skill folder (it must not exclude SKILL.md ). The publish workflow reads name + version from this file and skips any version already published. Bumping version is what ships a new release. See Contribute → Versioning for the npm version flow.

text: For each changed skill, the validator confirms all of the following. If this list and the validator script ( scripts/validate_skill.py ) ever disagree, the script wins. If you see a failure on a PR, this list maps directly to the checks: The SKILL.md starts with a closed YAML frontmatter block that parses as a mapping. name and description are present and non-empty. name is kebab-case, at most 64 characters, and matches the skill's directory name . description is at most 1024 characters and contains no angle brackets. No unexpected frontmatter keys are present (only name , description , owner , tags , license , allowed-tools , compatibility , metadata ). The body has an H1 title. All seven required sections are present: Use When , Don't Use When , Workflow , Rules , Examples , Edge Cases , References . None of those required sections is empty. The whole SKILL.md is at most 500 lines. Any bundled scripts/ , references/ , or assets/ directory is flat (no nested subdirectories). For a published skill under skills/ , a package.json sits beside the manifest with a valid name and a semver version , and does not pin a files whitelist. For a meta-skill under .github/skills/ , a missing package.json is allowed; if one is present it is held to the same rules.
